runs.name: DMC Global Inc.
runs.entry: Price **$5.66** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **20,540,949 shares** (one class, 10-Q cover for 2026-06-30, 0000034067-26-000048; issued 21,559,103 less 1,018,154 treasury and deferred-compensation shares, exact) = cap **$116.3M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y, 2026-10-09). Primary document the FY2025 10-K (0000034067-26-000009), with the 10-Q of 2026-07-29, the DEF 14A of 2026-03-31, the 8-Ks of 2026-03-05, 2026-04-27, 2026-05-14 and 2026-07-29, and the FY2020, FY2021 and FY2023 10-Ks; FY2025 operating cash $53,534 thousand cross-checked to the filed statement. Formerly Dynamic Materials Corp (renamed 2016); three businesses: Arcadia Products (architectural aluminum framing, 60% owned since 2021), DynaEnergetics (perforating systems for well completion) and NobelClad (explosion-welded clad plate). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs. Q1 IN narrowly, a company of parts read by its parts: DynaEnergetics decides at 56% of FY2021-FY2025 segment operating profit before Arcadia's 2024 goodwill charge (164% with it); NobelClad $66.9M, Arcadia -$114.0M with the charge ($27.7M without). **Q2 OUT** on DynaEnergetics, the castle shown filling in on the filer's own evidence: the FY2021 10-K says rivals' pre-wired carriers copy its patented features and no single patent is critical; lower pricing 'due to industry consolidation and a highly competitive core North American market' cost $16.2M of 2025 sales and prices fell again in Q2 2026; one customer 26% of consolidated 2025 sales (about 59% of the segment), and the three largest service companies make the product themselves; segment operating margin 22.2% (2019), 4.2%, 4.7%, 14.8%, 14.7%, 5.6%, 3.8% (2025) and 3.8% (first half 2026), gross margin 39.5% to 15.9%. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: featured Adjusted EBITDA and an adjusted net figure computed before the transfer to the 40% Arcadia holder, with incentive pay on Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Free Cash Flow; a stockholder rights plan extended to 2027-06-04; 2026 long-term awards paid partly in cash for lack of plan shares. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash (operating cash less stock pay less all capital spending) FY2021-FY2025 -$27.0M, $16.4M, $40.0M, $22.5M, $31.5M; central range **$11.77-$17.40** a share (all-equity, combined window 2022-2025 under the merger rule, acquisitions deducted, growth cut from +7.4% to sales growth of -4.5%), fair $7.72 all-equity ($6.88 equity-only); with the Arcadia put exercised at its floor, fair $5.57 ($5.28 equity-only); the literal 2021-2025 window, charging the $285.9M Arcadia purchase, gives no positive value. Not armed as an alert (box not OUT at Q7). The put on Arcadia's 40%: floor $187.08M (about $162.2M net of a note owed back), exercisable since 2026-09-06, up to 80% payable in a convertible Put Preferred the 10-Q says would likely give the holder majority voting control; against a $116.3M market value. Balance sheets FY2016-2026-06-30: equity $112M (2016) to $410M (2023) after about $149M of shares sold in 2021, then $242M (2025) after the $141.7M Arcadia goodwill write-off and $68.7M charged to carry the minority at its floor; retained earnings $146.6M (2023) to a $13.5M deficit (2025); inventory 13.5% of sales (2019) to 23.7% (2025), receivables flat near 15%; debt $59.1M against $28.6M cash at 2026-06-30, leverage 2.19x against a 3.0x maximum. Competitors: the 10-K names no rival by name; the analyst took the nearest SEC filers and said so: five-year operating margin DynaEnergetics 9.2%, Core Lab Production Enhancement 7.2%, Halliburton Completion and Production 18.3%; private perforating makers not read. Contamination declared by the analyst: one listing of `Test Runs/` by pattern returned other companies' file names (Del Monte, General Dynamics), not opened; DSGR commit subjects in git log; the memory index's queue lines; nothing used. Commits one per question, 061cd131 to 2d5550fd. Citations: the analyst's check 35 ids, 27 fragments, 0 problems; the dispatcher's script (`fold_cite_check.py`) 35 ids present, 23 fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) a put-able minority interest with a contractual floor is not in Q7's net-debt definition (borrowings and finance leases), and counting it moves the fair price from above the price to below it; (2) no rule for a consolidated subsidiary with a minority (the analyst deducted the cash paid to the minority by analogy with the equity-method rule); (3) a merger inside the window whose target's pre-merger years are not on file leaves fewer than five combined years; (4) specific (f)'s highest share of sales is ambiguous across a merger; (5) section B's five-year operating profit does not say whether an impairment counts; (6) the brief's competitor rule yields nothing when the 10-K names no rival. The 21% tax rate on the interest add-back is the analyst's own convention.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT on DynaEnergetics, the deciding part (56% of five-year segment profit): rivals copy its patented carriers, prices are being cut to consolidated customers who also make the product, and its margin fell from 22.2% (2019) to 3.8% (2025 and the first half of 2026). COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range $11.77-$17.40 all-equity, fair $7.72 ($5.57 with the Arcadia put at its $187M floor, a claim larger than the $116M market value) against $5.66 (not armed, box not OUT at Q7). The analyst asks whether a put-able minority interest belongs in Q7's net debt.
